bull_bear.body:
- Track record and reference base: close to 220 projects executed to date, with exhaustive experience in feasibility studies and detailed design engineering across water, renewable energy and infrastructure projects.
- Deep multi-disciplinary technical bench: 80+ experienced engineers across Civil, E&M, HM, Geology, Hydrology, GIS, Geophysics, Project Management, Cost Estimate and Financial Analysis, able to take large projects from concept to commissioning.
- Comprehensive whole-lifecycle service portfolio - design and engineering, due diligence and regulatory advisory, bid management, construction engineering, quality assurance and inspection - allowing end-to-end engagement on a single project.
- Geographic diversification: presence across 15+ Indian states plus international operations in Bhutan, Laos and Africa, with new international business won during FY2025-26 in Bhutan and Laos.
- Sector diversification beyond hydropower into pumped storage, solar, irrigation, tunnels and urban infrastructure, serving a broad client base of EPC contractors, PSUs, IPPs and other consultants.
- Experienced founder-led management: Promoter and Managing Director Mr. Subhash Chander Mittal has more than 42 years of engineering experience and has been on the Board since incorporation.
- Proficiency in industry-leading specialist engineering software (STAD Pro, ZWCAD, AutoCAD, Revit, Civil 3D, MIDAS, Relux, ETAP, Hammer OpenFlows, Unwedge, DIPS, RS2/RS3) plus proprietary geotechnical and structural applications.
- In-house specialised subsidiaries broadening the service line, including one company specialising in geophysical investigations.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Human-capital dependency - the business has no assets other than its engineers — DMR's delivery capacity is entirely people-led: 60 permanent employees as at 31 March 2026 for a consultancy that has executed close to 220 projects. Management states that 'our ability to attract, develop, retain, and effectively deploy a highly skilled workforce of engineering and management professionals significantly influences our operational efficiency, service quality, and long-term profitability', and the risk register's people row is mitigated only by 'the development of comprehensive career and talent development plans'. Loss of senior specialists directly removes revenue capacity and bid credibility.
- Diversification into capital-intensive, regulated adjacencies well outside the asset-light consultancy model — AGM Item No. 7 records that 'the Company has identified significant business opportunities in the areas of Engineering Consulting, EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) Services, Power Trading Services including cross-border power trading, and Renewable Energy Power Generation, Energy Storage and Transmission businesses, in accordance with the applicable guidelines, rules and regulations issued by CERC/SERC and other regulatory authorities.' EPC, power trading and generation carry balance-sheet, execution and CERC/SERC licensing exposures the current fee-based consultancy does not, and the Company discloses no capital commitment to fund them.
- Country, foreign-currency and cross-border exposure from international operations — The MD&A financial-risk row explicitly names 'Taxation Risks, Market Risk, Foreign Currency Risk, Credit Risk, Liquidity Risk, Operational Risk, Country Risk'. These are live rather than theoretical: operations run in Bhutan, Laos and Africa, a US subsidiary (DMR Consulting USA Inc., Cupertino) is held 100% but the investment into it 'is pending due to regulatory measures', and the newly identified opportunity set includes cross-border power trading. Mitigation is described only as a generic four-stage identify-analyse-decide-monitor process.
- Client credit and collection risk in a fee-based, project-linked model — Credit risk and liquidity risk are named in the MD&A financial-risk row. The revenue base is B2B and concentrated in EPC agencies, PSUs and IPPs whose own payment cycles are project- and approval-driven, so realisation timing sits outside the Company's control while its cost base (salaried engineers) is fixed.
- Employee health and safety exposure from remote-site and international field work — The risk register carries a dedicated Employee Health & Safety row, noting that a healthy and safe working environment affects productivity, retention and reputation. The exposure is structural for this business: during FY 2025-26 experts and engineers travelled to remote locations in Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Manipur, Mizoram, Bhutan, Laos and Africa, and the lender-engineering team travels extensively across India. Mitigation is limited to awareness and training programmes, physical/psychological support and medical insurance for permanent employees.
- Climate change as a threat to operations and personnel — The risk register states that 'climate change is a threat to the Company's infrastructure that may disrupt operations and potentially impact the safety and well-being of employees', mitigated by a business continuity policy and emergency response plans. For a firm whose assignments sit on Himalayan hydropower, dam and tunnel sites, weather and hydrological disruption is a direct project-delivery and site-access risk.
- Fraud, bribery and anti-corruption exposure in a PSU- and tender-driven client base — The register flags that 'non-compliance to ABAC requirements or fraud instances can expose an organization to reputational and financial damage', with integrity described as critical to safeguarding market confidence and client trust. The Company bids for PSU and government-linked infrastructure work in India and overseas, where procurement-integrity failures can result in disqualification as well as reputational loss. Mitigation is the DMR Business Code of Conduct plus an ABAC programme.
- Governance and board-transition risk around a founder-centred, family-represented board — A corporate-governance risk row is carried in the register, noting that governance failures 'can result in reputation loss and damage to stakeholder trust and business disruption', mitigated by periodical internal reviews, audits and regulatory-change presentations. The board is in the middle of a substantial transition - Mr. Man Mohan Madan appointed 28 February 2026, and Mr. Divay Mittal and Mr. Arvind Bhat on 9 May 2026, all still pending shareholder regularisation - while the promoter Managing Director and family members (Smt. Neelam Mittal, Whole-time Director; Mr. Divay Mittal) hold executive positions. The AR itself carries internal inconsistencies in these disclosures (Mr. Divay Mittal shown with two different DINs; director terms printed as 'five (2) years').

business.body: DMR provides engineering consultancy services from concept-to-commissioning across hydropower (small hydro, large hydro and pumped storage projects), dams, solar and renewable energy, water resources and irrigation, road and railway tunnels and urban infrastructure. Its offering spans strategic advisory and due diligence, feasibility reports and DPRs, geological, hydrological, hydraulic and geotechnical studies, detailed design and drawings, bid and construction engineering, project management and QA/QC and inspection services. The Company operates a business-to-business model, serving EPC agencies, PSUs, independent power producers (IPPs) and other consultants in both domestic and international markets.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Design & Engineering:** Topographical Surveys, Geotechnical Investigations, Geological Mapping, Feasibility Report, Detailed Project Report, Hydrological Studies, Hydraulic Design of Structures, Hydraulic Model Studies, Geotechnical Design of Surface & Underground Structures, Structural Design and Analysis, Concrete Technology & Grouting Technology, Numerical Analysis, Instrumentation Analysis, Detailed Design and Drawings
- **Bid Management & Construction Engineering:** Tender documents and BOQ, Construction Planning & Scheduling, Construction Management & Method Statements, Design & Engineering Support During Construction, Billing, Rate Analysis and Cost Estimates, Contract Management & Claims Management, Procurement Management, Project Management, Time Studies, Project Commissioning
- **Quality & Inspection:** QA/QC plans, Lab Testing, Quality Assurance at Site, Pre-dispatch Inspection, Third Party Inspection, Compliance Audit, Dam Safety & Inspections
- **Due Diligence & Regulatory:** Strategic Advisory, Due Diligence Studies, Project Development Services, Impact Assessment, Monitoring & Evaluation, Regulatory Support and Assessment, Environment Studies, Health & Safety

outlook.body:
- Pursue potential national and international business opportunities, and forge business partnerships with international partners.
- Consolidate the Company's position in pumped storage, hydro power, solar power, dam safety, plant technical audits and tunnel engineering opportunities.
- Build capacities around delivering project management consulting (PMC) services for hydro power, dams and tunnel projects.
- Leverage the knowledge of specialised engineering software in the delivery of assignments; teams are also embracing Artificial Intelligence in day-to-day work to bring efficiency.
- Grow the Company's specialised subsidiaries and associate companies so they complement the core delivery capability.
- Prepare the organisation for global project delivery, including international travel, as project owners and large contractors worldwide seek DMR's support.
- Overhaul the senior team profile with a blend of high-performing seniors and young talent, including the induction of new executive and non-executive directors into leadership roles to propel growth.
- Enter adjacent energy and infrastructure businesses: the AGM notice records that the Company has identified significant business opportunities in EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) services, power trading including cross-border power trading, renewable energy power generation, energy storage and transmission, alongside its existing engineering consulting - a material widening beyond the fee-based consultancy model.
- Long-term intent to become a global company with presence in both developed and developing economies within the coming 10 years.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: DMR is an asset-light engineering consultancy and discloses no manufacturing capacity, no plant additions and no rupee capex programme anywhere in this bundle; the named capital-commitments disclosure explicitly states that no capital commitment exists as at the financial-statement date. Expansion is therefore expressed as footprint, corporate structure and people. Structurally, the Company has built out subsidiaries to widen its service lines - as at March 31, 2026 it had three subsidiaries: DM Consulting Engineers Private Limited and DM Gates and Penstocks Private Limited (both Faridabad, Haryana, India) and DMR Consulting USA Inc. in Cupertino, United States of America; the corporate overview adds that 'we have established several subsidiary companies, including one company specializing in geophysical investigations, further diversifying our areas of service', and management proposes to further grow its specialised subsidiaries and associate companies to complement delivery. The overseas arm is not yet funded: as on March 31, 2026 the Company had made no foreign investment except into DMR Consulting USA Inc., and that investment 'is pending due to regulatory measures'. Geographically, service expansion continued beyond hydropower into pumped storage, solar, small hydro and irrigation projects, with domestic presence across 15+ states and international operations in Bhutan, Laos and Africa - new international business having been won during FY2025-26 notably in Bhutan and Laos. On physical footprint, the only facility change disclosed is that the business office now operates from a business campus at RPS 12th Avenue, Faridabad, located on NH-2 Mathura Road. Delivery capacity is headcount-led: 60 permanent employees as at 31 March 2026 (the strengths section cites a pool of 80+ experienced engineers), with talent acquisition described as building a pool 'capable of supporting its current operations as well as future expansion plans'. No commissioning dates, capacity additions, acquisitions or named capital projects are disclosed.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- International markets are the visible growth vector: the international business team won new business during the year notably in Bhutan and Laos, and operations now span Bhutan, Laos and Africa.
- End-market pull is described as coming from road and water tunnels, dams, small hydropower, renewable energy, power and pumped storage, with the Company's work tied to the themes of carbon reduction, energy transition, improved mobility and water security.
- Solar is served through a dedicated Lender Engineering team that travels extensively across India, including Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand.
- Hydropower assignments continue to draw engineers into remote geographies - Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Manipur and Mizoram.
- Management frames the Company as 'a mid-sized, diversified engineering consultancy ready to operate on a global scale' with a team strength of 60 staff, i.e. delivery capacity is people-led rather than asset-led.
- MD&A's own performance discussion: 'the Company recorded a decline of 2.01% in its revenue from operations ... The net profit of the Company also declined by 43.94%' in FY2025-26 versus FY2024-25 - a year of contraction against which the FY27 growth ambition is set.
- Auditors' key audit matter flags a receivables-driven watch-item: increasing challenges in the economy and operating environment during the year raised the risk of customer default, though management concluded no impairment allowance was required as at March 31, 2026.
- No formal MD&A 'Industry Structure / Outlook / Opportunities and Threats' narrative was present in the routed bundle - the MD&A material received is dominated by the risk-register table, internal controls and human-resources sections.
- "We are having robust order book at the end of the financial year 2025-26." - Chairman & Managing Director's message. No order-book value, composition or execution period is quantified anywhere in this bundle.
- "Ambitious targets for order book and revenue growth have been set for 2026-27." - order-book growth is stated as an FY27 objective but is left unquantified.

one_liner.body: DMR Engineering Limited (formerly DMR Hydroengineering & Infrastructures Limited) is a BSE SME-listed, asset-light engineering consultancy providing concept-to-commissioning design, due-diligence and project-management services across hydropower, pumped storage, dams, tunnels and renewables, having …

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: DMR provides engineering consultancy services from concept-to-commissioning across hydropower (small hydro, large hydro and pumped storage projects), dams, solar and renewable energy, water resources and irrigation, road and railway tunnels and urban infrastructure. Its offering spans strategic advisory and due diligence, feasibility reports and DPRs, geological, hydrological, hydraulic and geotechnical studies, detailed design and drawings, bid and construction engineering, project management and QA/QC and inspection services. The Company operates a business-to-business model, serving EPC agencies, PSUs, independent power producers (IPPs) and other consultants in both domestic and international markets.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- DMR Consulting USA Inc. — subsidiary: Wholly owned - extent of shareholding 100%. Based in Cupertino, United States of America; reporting currency USD, reporting period April-March. The Company's investment into it was still pending as at March 31, 2026 due to regulatory measures. Also named in the related-party note as a Subsidiary.
- DM Consulting Engineers Private Limited — subsidiary: Extent of shareholding 60%. Faridabad, Haryana, India; reporting currency INR, reporting period April-March. Named in the related-party note as a Subsidiary, with 'Consulting Services' transactions and a closing balance outstanding.
- DM Gates and Penstocks Private Limited — subsidiary: Extent of shareholding 45%. Faridabad, Haryana, India; reporting currency INR, reporting period April-March. Classification is inconsistent within the report: the Board's Report and Form AOC-1 Part A present it among the Company's three subsidiaries, while the related-party disclosure lists it under 'Associates'.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- International markets are the visible growth vector: the international business team won new business during the year notably in Bhutan and Laos, and operations now span Bhutan, Laos and Africa.
- End-market pull is described as coming from road and water tunnels, dams, small hydropower, renewable energy, power and pumped storage, with the Company's work tied to the themes of carbon reduction, energy transition, improved mobility and water security.
- Solar is served through a dedicated Lender Engineering team that travels extensively across India, including Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand.
- Hydropower assignments continue to draw engineers into remote geographies - Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Manipur and Mizoram.
- Management frames the Company as 'a mid-sized, diversified engineering consultancy ready to operate on a global scale' with a team strength of 60 staff, i.e. delivery capacity is people-led rather than asset-led.
- MD&A's own performance discussion: 'the Company recorded a decline of 2.01% in its revenue from operations ... The net profit of the Company also declined by 43.94%' in FY2025-26 versus FY2024-25 - a year of contraction against which the FY27 growth ambition is set.
- Auditors' key audit matter flags a receivables-driven watch-item: increasing challenges in the economy and operating environment during the year raised the risk of customer default, though management concluded no impairment allowance was required as at March 31, 2026.
- No formal MD&A 'Industry Structure / Outlook / Opportunities and Threats' narrative was present in the routed bundle - the MD&A material received is dominated by the risk-register table, internal controls and human-resources sections.
- "We are having robust order book at the end of the financial year 2025-26." - Chairman & Managing Director's message. No order-book value, composition or execution period is quantified anywhere in this bundle.
- "Ambitious targets for order book and revenue growth have been set for 2026-27." - order-book growth is stated as an FY27 objective but is left unquantified.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Pursue potential national and international business opportunities, and forge business partnerships with international partners.
- Consolidate the Company's position in pumped storage, hydro power, solar power, dam safety, plant technical audits and tunnel engineering opportunities.
- Build capacities around delivering project management consulting (PMC) services for hydro power, dams and tunnel projects.
- Leverage the knowledge of specialised engineering software in the delivery of assignments; teams are also embracing Artificial Intelligence in day-to-day work to bring efficiency.
- Grow the Company's specialised subsidiaries and associate companies so they complement the core delivery capability.
- Prepare the organisation for global project delivery, including international travel, as project owners and large contractors worldwide seek DMR's support.
- Overhaul the senior team profile with a blend of high-performing seniors and young talent, including the induction of new executive and non-executive directors into leadership roles to propel growth.
- Enter adjacent energy and infrastructure businesses: the AGM notice records that the Company has identified significant business opportunities in EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) services, power trading including cross-border power trading, renewable energy power generation, energy storage and transmission, alongside its existing engineering consulting - a material widening beyond the fee-based consultancy model.
- Long-term intent to become a global company with presence in both developed and developing economies within the coming 10 years.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: DMR is an asset-light engineering consultancy and discloses no manufacturing capacity, no plant additions and no rupee capex programme anywhere in this bundle; the named capital-commitments disclosure explicitly states that no capital commitment exists as at the financial-statement date. Expansion is therefore expressed as footprint, corporate structure and people. Structurally, the Company has built out subsidiaries to widen its service lines - as at March 31, 2026 it had three subsidiaries: DM Consulting Engineers Private Limited and DM Gates and Penstocks Private Limited (both Faridabad, Haryana, India) and DMR Consulting USA Inc. in Cupertino, United States of America; the corporate overview adds that 'we have established several subsidiary companies, including one company specializing in geophysical investigations, further diversifying our areas of service', and management proposes to further grow its specialised subsidiaries and associate companies to complement delivery. The overseas arm is not yet funded: as on March 31, 2026 the Company had made no foreign investment except into DMR Consulting USA Inc., and that investment 'is pending due to regulatory measures'. Geographically, service expansion continued beyond hydropower into pumped storage, solar, small hydro and irrigation projects, with domestic presence across 15+ states and international operations in Bhutan, Laos and Africa - new international business having been won during FY2025-26 notably in Bhutan and Laos. On physical footprint, the only facility change disclosed is that the business office now operates from a business campus at RPS 12th Avenue, Faridabad, located on NH-2 Mathura Road. Delivery capacity is headcount-led: 60 permanent employees as at 31 March 2026 (the strengths section cites a pool of 80+ experienced engineers), with talent acquisition described as building a pool 'capable of supporting its current operations as well as future expansion plans'. No commissioning dates, capacity additions, acquisitions or named capital projects are disclosed.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Track record and reference base: close to 220 projects executed to date, with exhaustive experience in feasibility studies and detailed design engineering across water, renewable energy and infrastructure projects.
- Deep multi-disciplinary technical bench: 80+ experienced engineers across Civil, E&M, HM, Geology, Hydrology, GIS, Geophysics, Project Management, Cost Estimate and Financial Analysis, able to take large projects from concept to commissioning.
- Comprehensive whole-lifecycle service portfolio - design and engineering, due diligence and regulatory advisory, bid management, construction engineering, quality assurance and inspection - allowing end-to-end engagement on a single project.
- Geographic diversification: presence across 15+ Indian states plus international operations in Bhutan, Laos and Africa, with new international business won during FY2025-26 in Bhutan and Laos.
- Sector diversification beyond hydropower into pumped storage, solar, irrigation, tunnels and urban infrastructure, serving a broad client base of EPC contractors, PSUs, IPPs and other consultants.
- Experienced founder-led management: Promoter and Managing Director Mr. Subhash Chander Mittal has more than 42 years of engineering experience and has been on the Board since incorporation.
- Proficiency in industry-leading specialist engineering software (STAD Pro, ZWCAD, AutoCAD, Revit, Civil 3D, MIDAS, Relux, ETAP, Hammer OpenFlows, Unwedge, DIPS, RS2/RS3) plus proprietary geotechnical and structural applications.
- In-house specialised subsidiaries broadening the service line, including one company specialising in geophysical investigations.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Human-capital dependency - the business has no assets other than its engineers — DMR's delivery capacity is entirely people-led: 60 permanent employees as at 31 March 2026 for a consultancy that has executed close to 220 projects. Management states that 'our ability to attract, develop, retain, and effectively deploy a highly skilled workforce of engineering and management professionals significantly influences our operational efficiency, service quality, and long-term profitability', and the risk register's people row is mitigated only by 'the development of comprehensive career and talent development plans'. Loss of senior specialists directly removes revenue capacity and bid credibility.
- Diversification into capital-intensive, regulated adjacencies well outside the asset-light consultancy model — AGM Item No. 7 records that 'the Company has identified significant business opportunities in the areas of Engineering Consulting, EPC (Engineering, Procurement and Construction) Services, Power Trading Services including cross-border power trading, and Renewable Energy Power Generation, Energy Storage and Transmission businesses, in accordance with the applicable guidelines, rules and regulations issued by CERC/SERC and other regulatory authorities.' EPC, power trading and generation carry balance-sheet, execution and CERC/SERC licensing exposures the current fee-based consultancy does not, and the Company discloses no capital commitment to fund them.
- Country, foreign-currency and cross-border exposure from international operations — The MD&A financial-risk row explicitly names 'Taxation Risks, Market Risk, Foreign Currency Risk, Credit Risk, Liquidity Risk, Operational Risk, Country Risk'. These are live rather than theoretical: operations run in Bhutan, Laos and Africa, a US subsidiary (DMR Consulting USA Inc., Cupertino) is held 100% but the investment into it 'is pending due to regulatory measures', and the newly identified opportunity set includes cross-border power trading. Mitigation is described only as a generic four-stage identify-analyse-decide-monitor process.
- Client credit and collection risk in a fee-based, project-linked model — Credit risk and liquidity risk are named in the MD&A financial-risk row. The revenue base is B2B and concentrated in EPC agencies, PSUs and IPPs whose own payment cycles are project- and approval-driven, so realisation timing sits outside the Company's control while its cost base (salaried engineers) is fixed.
- Employee health and safety exposure from remote-site and international field work — The risk register carries a dedicated Employee Health & Safety row, noting that a healthy and safe working environment affects productivity, retention and reputation. The exposure is structural for this business: during FY 2025-26 experts and engineers travelled to remote locations in Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Manipur, Mizoram, Bhutan, Laos and Africa, and the lender-engineering team travels extensively across India. Mitigation is limited to awareness and training programmes, physical/psychological support and medical insurance for permanent employees.
- Climate change as a threat to operations and personnel — The risk register states that 'climate change is a threat to the Company's infrastructure that may disrupt operations and potentially impact the safety and well-being of employees', mitigated by a business continuity policy and emergency response plans. For a firm whose assignments sit on Himalayan hydropower, dam and tunnel sites, weather and hydrological disruption is a direct project-delivery and site-access risk.
- Fraud, bribery and anti-corruption exposure in a PSU- and tender-driven client base — The register flags that 'non-compliance to ABAC requirements or fraud instances can expose an organization to reputational and financial damage', with integrity described as critical to safeguarding market confidence and client trust. The Company bids for PSU and government-linked infrastructure work in India and overseas, where procurement-integrity failures can result in disqualification as well as reputational loss. Mitigation is the DMR Business Code of Conduct plus an ABAC programme.
- Governance and board-transition risk around a founder-centred, family-represented board — A corporate-governance risk row is carried in the register, noting that governance failures 'can result in reputation loss and damage to stakeholder trust and business disruption', mitigated by periodical internal reviews, audits and regulatory-change presentations. The board is in the middle of a substantial transition - Mr. Man Mohan Madan appointed 28 February 2026, and Mr. Divay Mittal and Mr. Arvind Bhat on 9 May 2026, all still pending shareholder regularisation - while the promoter Managing Director and family members (Smt. Neelam Mittal, Whole-time Director; Mr. Divay Mittal) hold executive positions. The AR itself carries internal inconsistencies in these disclosures (Mr. Divay Mittal shown with two different DINs; director terms printed as 'five (2) years').
